hints.title: Do not stop at one angle
hints.body: tanx=3 has more solutions than x=60∘. Tangent repeats every 180∘.
hints.recap: A correct sample angle need not describe all solutions.
hints.pitfall: A true numerical answer can still have an incomplete proof.
hints.pause: Write all possible <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> using an integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Track the whole angle family
hints.body: Use tangent’s period to write every x as the standard acute solution plus an integer multiple of 180∘, then double the entire expression.
hints.recap: A multiple-angle expression must include the repeated-period term.
hints.pitfall: Doubling only the first angle loses other possible inputs.
hints.pause: Compare the resulting spacing with sine’s period.

recall.reminder: A multiple-angle expression must include the repeated-period term.

hints.title: Separate the two questions
hints.body: First decide how many different output values the full family gives; separately check whether the student’s written reasoning justifies that conclusion.
hints.recap: Truth of an answer and adequacy of its proof are separate.
hints.pitfall: Different input angles need not produce different sine values.
hints.pause: Complete both checks before choosing a statement.

recall.reminder: Truth of an answer and adequacy of its proof are separate.

solution:
Every solution of tanx=3 has the form x=60∘+180∘n for an integer n. Therefore 2x=120∘+360∘n.

Since sine repeats after 360∘, all these angles give sin(2x)=sin120∘=32. Thus the displayed value is the only possible one.

However, the student’s reasoning checked just x=60∘ and did not justify the other tangent solutions. B correctly identifies the unique answer and the gap in its justification.
knowledgePattern: Separate correctness of a trig value from completeness of its proof
